statement: In Oklahoma you petition the district court in the county where you live for a change of name, as long as you have lived in that county for more than 30 days.
detail: Oklahoma law bars anyone required to register under the Oklahoma Sex Offenders Registration Act from petitioning for a name change. If the person is a minor, the petition is brought by a guardian or next friend instead.

cost.note: The statute doesn't set a specific filing fee; contact the district court clerk in your county for the current amount.

source.title: Oklahoma Statutes Citationized — 12 O.S. § 1631, Right to Petition for Change of Name

topic: Oklahoma driver's license and ID name change
statement: You cannot change the name on your Oklahoma driver's license or ID card online. For a name change, you visit a licensed operator or Service Oklahoma (SOK) location in person to request a duplicate, and a new credential is mailed to you for $25.
detail: This help-center article doesn't list which documents to bring for a name change specifically; contact Service Oklahoma or a licensed operator for current requirements.

cost.note: The $25 is Service Oklahoma's standard duplicate-credential fee — the same one charged for other changes, not a fee specific to name changes.

source.title: Service Oklahoma Help Center — How can I make changes to the information on my Driver's License card?

topic: Oklahoma driver's license and ID sex/gender designation
statement: Service Oklahoma's own list of driver's license and ID services does not include a way to change the sex or gender marker on a license or ID card.
detail: This page lists every standard driver's-license and ID service Service Oklahoma offers — a new license, renewals, REAL ID, address updates, and more — and none of them is described as a sex or gender-designation change. Read the current official page yourself, and don't assume a route exists that isn't listed there.

statement: A legal name change on an Oklahoma birth record is not treated as a minor correction — the Oklahoma State Department of Health says a District Court order is required, and you should contact your local court clerk or an attorney for help.
detail: Small mistakes, like a misspelled name, can go through a $15 application plus a $25 amendment fee instead, with either an administrative order or a district court order. But an actual legal name change, an adoption, or a paternity update all require a District Court order first, and this process can take up to 4 months.

cost.note: The page doesn't state a fee for the District Court order path itself; the $15 application fee and $25 amendment fee it lists apply to the separate minor-correction process.

timeline.note: This is the department's stated ceiling for legal changes generally (adoptions, paternity, and delayed registrations included), not a name-change-specific estimate.

source.title: Oklahoma State Department of Health — Amending an Oklahoma Birth or Death Record

statement: Oklahoma law says every birth certificate amended under this statute must show the sex identified at the time of birth, and it cannot be amended to display gender identity, a nonbinary designation, or the letter "X".
detail: This rule applies to any amendment made under 63 O.S. § 1-321, not only ones related to gender. Oklahoma law describes no court-order or administrative process for changing the sex designation on a birth certificate to match your gender identity. If you were told a route exists, verify it directly with the Oklahoma State Department of Health before relying on it.

source.title: Oklahoma Statutes Citationized — 63 O.S. § 1-321, Amendment of Certificate or Record
